content: 1. A study conducted in Agusan del Sur, Philippines, focused on the administration of mass drug treatments to eliminate lymphatic filariasis, as reported in Parasites and Vectors in 2008. 2. Research by Babu BV and Nath N in Orissa, India, examined the attitudes of program partners involved in the lymphatic filariasis elimination initiative, published in the Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 2004. 3. Another study by Babu BV and Kar SK in Orissa, India, explored the coverage, compliance, and operational challenges of mass drug administration during the lymphatic filariasis elimination program, as detailed in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2004. 4. Babu BV also conducted a qualitative study on adverse reactions to mass treatment for lymphatic filariasis in Orissa, India, with findings published in the Asian Pacific Journal of Tropical Medicine in 2010. 5. Baker MC and colleagues investigated the integration of the lymphatic filariasis elimination program into primary healthcare in the Dominican Republic, highlighting its impact in the International Journal of Health Planning and Management in 2007. 6. A qualitative study by da-Costa Vroom FB and colleagues identified data reporting constraints during mass drug administration for lymphatic filariasis in two districts in Ghana, published in SAGE Open Medicine in 2015. 7. Hussain MA and colleagues examined barriers to coverage and compliance in mass drug administration for lymphatic filariasis elimination in a coastal state of India, as reported in Infectious Diseases of Poverty in 2014. 8. King JD and colleagues studied methods to improve community participation in the elimination of lymphatic filariasis in American Samoa, with results published in Acta Tropica in 2011. 9. Kisoka W and colleagues conducted a qualitative study on the dilemmas of community-directed mass drug administration for lymphatic filariasis control in urban and rural Tanzania, as reported in the Journal of Biosocial Science in 2016. 10. Another study by Kisoka WJ and colleagues explored community perceptions of mass drug administration for lymphatic filariasis control in rural and urban Tanzania, published in the Journal of Biosocial Science in 2016. 11. Krentel A and Aunger R introduced a novel method called causal chain mapping to analyze treatment compliance decisions related to lymphatic filariasis elimination in Alor, Indonesia, as detailed in Health Policy and Planning in 2011. 12. Njomo DW and colleagues investigated factors motivating community drug distributors in Kenya's lymphatic filariasis elimination program, with findings published in the Southern African Journal of Epidemiology & Infection in 2012. 13. Another study by Njomo DW and colleagues focused on increasing coverage of mass drug administration for lymphatic filariasis elimination in an urban setting, specifically Malindi Town, Kenya, as reported in PLOS ONE in 2014. 14. Wynd S and colleagues conducted a qualitative analysis of the impact of a lymphatic filariasis elimination program using mass drug administration on Misima Island, Papua New Guinea, published in the Filaria Journal in 2007. 15. The World Bank provided data on countries and economies in 2016, which was cited in the context of lymphatic filariasis elimination efforts. 16. WHO developed guidelines for alternative mass drug administration regimens for lymphatic filariasis elimination, with a planning proposal submitted to the WHO Guideline Review Committee in March 2016. 17. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported progress toward the elimination of onchocerciasis in the Americas from 1993 to 2012, as detailed in the MMWR in 2013. 18. WHO documented Ecuador's progress toward verifying the elimination of onchocerciasis in the Americas, as published in the Weekly Epidemiological Record in 2014. 19. Higazi TB and colleagues reported on the interruption of Onchocerca volvulus transmission in the Abu Hamed focus, Sudan, as detailed in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2013. 20. Katabarwa MN and colleagues demonstrated the interruption of onchocerciasis transmission in the Wadelai focus of northwestern Uganda, as published in the Journal of Parasitology Research in 2012. 21. Coffeng LE and colleagues modeled the impact of increasing ivermectin mass treatment frequency for African onchocerciasis elimination, with findings published in PLOS ONE in 2014. 22. Modeling studies on the impact and costs of semiannual mass drug administration for accelerated lymphatic filariasis elimination were published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2013. 23. Research on the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of co-administered diethylcarbamazine, albendazole, and ivermectin for treating bancroftian filariasis was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2016. 24. A systematic review of mass chemotherapy options for lymphatic filariasis control was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2005. 25. The Cochrane Collaboration updated its guidelines for systematic reviews in 2011, providing a framework for evidence-based research. 26. The GRADE Working Group updated its handbook for grading the quality of evidence and strength of recommendations in October 2013. 27. Noyes J and colleagues discussed qualitative research methods in Cochrane reviews, as outlined in the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions in 2008. 28. Ames HG and Lewin S synthesized qualitative evidence on parents' and caregivers' views of communication about routine childhood vaccination, as reported in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2016. 29. Carlsen B and colleagues conducted a meta-synthesis of general practitioners' attitudes toward clinical practice guidelines, published in the British Journal of General Practice in 2007. 30. Glenton C and colleagues synthesized qualitative evidence on barriers and facilitators to implementing lay health worker programs for maternal and child health, as reported in The Cochrane Library in 2013. 31. Munro SA and colleagues systematically reviewed qualitative research on patient adherence to tuberculosis treatment, with findings published in PLOS Medicine in 2007. 32. WHO provided evidence summaries on health system interventions, as cited in 2017. 33. Gopinathan U and colleagues conducted a multi-country case study synthesis on implementing large-scale health workforce programs in lowand middle-income settings, published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2014. 34. Muloliwa AM and colleagues identified health system barriers and facilitators to scaling up communication for childhood vaccination in low-income settings, as reported in 2017. 35. Oku A and colleagues studied factors affecting the implementation of childhood vaccination communication strategies in Nigeria, with findings published in BMC Public Health in 2017. 36. Glenton C and colleagues expanded the evidence base for global health system recommendations, as detailed in Implementation Science in 2016. 37. Lewin S and colleagues reviewed the role of lay health workers in primary and community healthcare for maternal and child health and infectious disease management, as reported in The Cochrane Library in 2010. 38. Research on the efficacy of single-dose combinations of albendazole, ivermectin, and diethylcarbamazine for treating bancroftian filariasis was published in Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1998.
